clue.text: Quick bowling? It's too hurried!

parts.note: a set of six balls in cricket followed by speed suggests the noun for excessive rush

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator complains that a bowler is rushing his deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names excessive speed or rashness, acting before proper thought.

clue.text: A little water spirit

explanation.surface: A small splash of water seems to hold a ghostly being.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian drink's name literally means little water, and it is a distilled liquor.

clue.text: Smoky old capital

parts.note: the Scots word for smoky forms part of the traditional nickname of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A grimy historic city wreathed in chimney smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh, Scotland's capital, was nicknamed Auld Reekie, old smoky, for its coal smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots adjective meaning smoky, best known from Edinburgh's nickname.

clue.text: Compose some notes

indicators.note: to compose is to arrange material, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician jots down a few notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical sounds of particular pitch, which a composer sets down.

clue.text: Encountered a doctor versed in the supernatural

definitions.note: the definition is a description; the answer is a person so versed

parts.note: met means encountered
a physician is a medical doctor

explanation.surface: Someone met a medic with an interest in the occult.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosopher of being and the beyond, someone who studies matters outside physical nature.

clue.text: Enrage arsonist with ceremonial vessel

parts.note: to incense someone is to enrage them
an arsonist is one who burns things

explanation.surface: Someone infuriates a fire-raiser using a church vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the fragrant stuff but here is the verb to enrage.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer, the container for burning fragrant resin in religious rites.

clue.text: Death toll due to simplistic navigation technique

parts.note: death suggests the state of being dead
a toll is a charge or reckoning to be paid

explanation.surface: A ship's fatalities blamed on crude navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimating position from speed, heading and time elapsed, without fixes from landmarks or stars.

clue.text: Wrap up badly and salute with cap

indicators.note: doing something badly scrambles it, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A soldier fumbles a salute while wearing a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something in a small case or shell.

clue.text: Inadequate performer in nude order

indicators.note: in with order behind it signals the letters are to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A poor actor appears naked on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does too little, falling short of what is needed.

clue.text: Plaintain cooked up by the AA in the back of a cab

indicators.note: in places the letters of the motoring organisation around the next piece

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association

indicators.note: taking the back of the word first reads cab from its end

explanation.surface: Bananas prepared by the breakdown service in the back of a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association; it goes around BAC, cab read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Philippine banana relative grown for Manila hemp fibre.

clue.text: The serious end of a boat

explanation.surface: The grim rear part of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Means severe in manner, and also the rear part of a ship.

clue.text: Go over and select again for the country

explanation.surface: Review and re-pick a player for the national side.
explanation.walkthrough: To cap a player is to select them for a national team.
explanation.definitionFit: Means summarise, and also (re-cap) to pick again for an international side.

clue.text: Go make up French road, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arrive in some unspecified rearranged order

parts.note: rue is French for street or road

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply cosmetics on a street in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cosmetic for the cheeks, a type of facial cosmetic.

clue.text: French vintage wine and bottle

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or vintage of wine
et is French for and, the French carrying over

explanation.surface: A French vintage and its bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass container for oil or vinegar at table.

clue.text: Pick the fat one

explanation.surface: Choose the overweight one.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for is to choose, and plump also means rounded or chubby.

clue.text: Split from mentally ill person

explanation.surface: Someone separating from a disturbed individual.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived prefix means split, and the informal term labels someone with schizophrenia.

clue.text: Female puppy?

parts.note: a Scots word for girl, also the name of a famous film collie

explanation.surface: A young girl dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for girl, and also the name of a famous screen collie.

first takes only the opening letter of the word growl

explanation.definitionFit: Failing to win, as in a game going against you.

clue.text: Premature end of bromide mix causes one to dwell on disease

definitions.text: causes one to dwell on disease
definitions.note: an adjective phrase described as a cause

indicators.note: mix tells us the remaining letters are stirred up
cutting short its end means the final letter of bromide is lopped

explanation.surface: A sedative cut short makes someone obsess over illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premature end of' drops E from BROMIDE; 'mix' rearranges BROMID.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhealthily preoccupied with death, gloom and illness.

clue.text: Prevent the pots being returned to the East

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word pots is read backwards

explanation.surface: Stop crockery being sent back eastwards.

clue.text: Take the pretty route to see Nick, we hear

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective in the phrase scenic route

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: the phrase see Nick said aloud

explanation.surface: Advice to drive the long way round to visit a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Picturesque, offering attractive views of the landscape.

clue.text: Bond character does the occasional bit of other work

definitions.text: the occasional bit of other work

explanation.surface: A spy-film henchman takes on casual labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddjob is the bowler-hatted henchman in the James Bond film Goldfinger.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain in Goldfinger, and an informal term for a minor casual task.

clue.text: It's sticky and in poor taste

explanation.surface: Something both gluey and vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Means slightly adhesive, as wet paint is, and also cheap or vulgar.

clue.text: Country bumpkin carries burden for student

parts.note: a yoke is a burden or load
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A rustic shoulders a load for a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive rural person, a rustic.

clue.text: It may serve as poetry

explanation.surface: A line suggesting something might work as poems.

clue.text: Minister in six-car pile-up

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clergyman caught in a motorway crash of six vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest, a clergyman.

clue.text: Do riders wear this coat for chopping potato

parts.note: hacking means chopping roughly
a jacket potato is one baked in its skin, the skin being its jacket

explanation.surface: Asking whether horse riders wear a coat for cutting up spuds.
explanation.walkthrough: A jacket potato is a baked potato in its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweed riding coat with slanted pockets and vents, worn on horseback.

clue.text: Flier may boycott prison

explanation.surface: An aviator may refuse to deal with a jail.
